application_credentials.description:
Parcels signs in with your own app. The client ID decides the provider, so you can add credentials for both.

**Outlook.com**: in [Microsoft Entra app registrations]({microsoft_console_url}), register an app for personal Microsoft accounts only, add the Web redirect URI `{redirect_url}`, create a client secret and add the delegated Microsoft Graph permissions Mail.Read and User.Read.

**Gmail**: in the [Google Cloud console]({google_console_url}), enable the [Gmail API]({gmail_api_url}), set up the OAuth consent screen with the gmail.readonly scope, and create an OAuth client of type Web application with the redirect URI `{redirect_url}`. Publish the app to production, or Google signs you out every 7 days.

parser_outdated.title: Shipping e-mails from {sender} aren't understood
parser_outdated.description:
Parcels couldn't read several recent shipping e-mails from {sender}. The sender may have changed its e-mails, or uses a layout Parcels doesn't know. The e-mails are waiting for review on the Parcels page, where you can add their details by hand.

If this keeps happening, check for an update of Parcels. This issue goes away when an e-mail from {sender} is understood again.

ai_unavailable.title: The local AI isn't available
ai_unavailable.description:
Parcels couldn't use the AI task entity chosen in its options. E-mails for the AI wait in the queue and go to review if the AI stays unavailable.

Check that the Ollama app and the Ollama integration are running. This issue goes away after the next successful AI call.

ai_task_refused.title: The chosen AI task isn't local
ai_task_refused.description:
Parcels only sends e-mails to an AI task entity of the Ollama integration whose model runs on this Home Assistant. The chosen AI task entity failed this check (reason: {reason}), so no e-mail was sent to it and the AI is paused.

Choose a local Ollama AI task entity in the Parcels options, or set the AI mode to off.
